goals: Mechanistic: characterize how surface/subsurface water partitioning (ET, surface runoff, drainage/recharge, snowpack) varies across the basin's elevation-and-soil structure
Validation: compare simulated snowpack against SNOTEL and simulated runoff against USGS gauges where those observations exist in-domain

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves the water/energy balance and snowpack at each sampled location; a stratified spatial sample spans the basin's heterogeneity.

answerable: Soil-texture control on water partitioning across sampled locations
Point-scale snowpack simulation at SNOTEL locations (SWE output exists) given adequate forcing
Relative partitioning behavior of columns under a common baseline forcing

not_answerable.aspect: Elevation/climate (lapse-rate, rain-snow, orographic) control on partitioning
not_answerable.why: Framework drives all columns with uniform forcing; a column set stratified by elevation under uniform forcing varies by SOIL, not by elevation-driven climate, so the elevation mechanism cannot be isolated.

not_answerable.aspect: Quantitative validation against USGS streamflow gauges
not_answerable.why: ELM columns produce local runoff/drainage fluxes; comparing to a gauge requires routing and aggregation over the contributing area, which the single-column stack does not perform.

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation band x dominant soil), transition-oversampled
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 5 elevation bands x 2 dominant soil classes = 10 baseline cells; add 2 light replicates in the 1200-1800 m rain-snow transition where partitioning is most sensitive. Small, spanning design rather than a dense grid; this is the smallest set that covers the elevation-soil cross-structure.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns in the 1200-1800 m rain-snow transition (steepest gradient in snow/runoff behavior and where future forcing-downscaling would matter most); place valley-bottom/riparian columns on fine soils to capture drainage/recharge, upland columns on coarse soils.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 extra columns in the transition band to sample within-band soil variability where the signal is strongest.

sampling_plan.reason: Baseline low-elevation partitioning; captures riparian fine-soil drainage/recharge vs upland coarse soils.

sampling_plan.group: lower montane (900-1200 m), fine + coarse soils
sampling_plan.reason: Bridges valley to transition; samples soil control below the snow line.

sampling_plan.group: rain-snow transition lower (1200-1500 m), fine + coarse + 1 replicate
sampling_plan.reason: Steep partitioning gradient; oversampled to resolve soil variability where snow/melt behavior turns over.

sampling_plan.group: rain-snow transition upper (1500-1800 m), fine + coarse + 1 replicate
sampling_plan.reason: Upper transition where SWE and melt-driven runoff dominate; oversampled for the same reason.
High-elevation snow accumulation zone; anchors the cold end of the gradient.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — place/associate a validation column at each in-domain SNOTEL site and compare simulated SWE time series to the station record
validation_design.metric: bias, RMSE, peak-SWE timing error, melt-out date error
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — equals number of in-domain SNOTEL stations (data-dictated)

validation_design.comparison: aggregated — NOT directly comparable from single columns; requires routing/aggregation of column runoff over the gauge's contributing area before comparison
validation_design.metric: bias, NSE, correlation (only once routing exists)
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — equals number of in-domain gauges (data-dictated)

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline forcing (1980-2018 available; representative multi-year period), native gridded soil per column

requires_capabilities.why: To make elevation act through temperature/precip/snow rather than only soil; required to attribute partitioning differences to elevation.
requires_capabilities.blocks: The core elevation-band mechanism the request asks for.

requires_capabilities.why: To convert per-column runoff/drainage into a comparable hydrograph at a gauge.
To pin validation columns to in-domain SNOTEL sites and load SWE records.
Downstream expander needs a DEM to place columns into the defined elevation bands.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Concrete point generation from these rules.

requires_capabilities.why: To assign dominant soil class per column for the soil stratification axis.
Snowpack and soil moisture states need equilibration before the analysis period.

assumptions: Multiple in-domain SNOTEL stations exist and span a range of elevations for co-located snow validation.
USGS gauges are in-domain but validation is deferred until routing/aggregation exists.
A representative multi-year subperiod of 1980-2018 is used as baseline forcing; exact years set downstream.
'Dominant coarse' and 'dominant fine' soil classes will be resolved from the gridded soil raster by the expander; specific textures are not invented here.
open_questions: How many in-domain SNOTEL stations and USGS gauges are actually present, and at what elevations?
Is elevation-downscaled forcing planned? If not, the campaign should be framed as a SOIL-control study, not an elevation study.
Should the analysis period target a specific climatology (e.g. wet vs dry years) or a long-term baseline?
